text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: multiple services failing to complete KMS signing during startup (region: eu-west1). Alert: signing_errors > 5% across instances in the last 2m. Case created: CLOUD-CASE-90827

maya: seeing a bunch of pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff on staging and a few hostnames in prod failing healthchecks. Logs show KMS returns 503 and timeouts during initial key fetch.

sam: confirmed on prod-cluster-3. startup container logs: 
```
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z service init: requesting key from kms.googleapis.com
2026-03-15T10:02:13Z ERROR signing: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = "503 Service Unavailable"
2026-03-15T10:02:20Z ERROR signing: context deadline exceeded
```

jack: impacted surfaces: token signing for inbound request auth (affects Dedicated onboarding), and initial service bootstrap that verifies certs. Some customers on Dedicated had failed deploys. Hosted API routing still serving steady but edge auth latency increased ~300ms for some requests.

maya: paging @sam @jack oncall. Any quick mitigations? Can we flip to cached-key fallback?

sam: yes, we have a cached local signing key used for emergency in older releases. It's off by default in runtime V2. I can push a canary patch to enable cached fallback for startup only (env var: REDWOOD_KMS_FALLBACK=startup-allow). That should let services come up without contacting KMS for first N minutes while we sort provider.

devops-ana: creating rollback-safe config. Suggest: set REDWOOD_KMS_RETRY=8 REDWOOD_KMS_TIMEOUT_MS=8000 and enable REDWOOD_KMS_FALLBACK=startup-allow. Will patch via k8s patch with maxUnavailable 1.

infra-ops: opened support ticket with GCP KMS and escalated to SE. Support replied same: "Investigating internal control plane throttling; recommend retry/backoff and local caching while we remediate." Case ID CLOUD-CASE-90827. ETA unknown.

maya: ok please run the patch on staging first and confirm startup success, then do prod canary (10% nodes)

sam: applying patch to staging now: 
```
kubectl -n redwood set env ds/runtime REDWOOD_KMS_FALLBACK=startup-allow REDWOOD_KMS_RETRY=8 REDWOOD_KMS_TIMEOUT_MS=8000
```

jack: also adding temporary routing rule: prefer us-central1 KMS endpoint for cross-region calls (less noisy) via runtime override until provider stabilizes. We'll keep EU pinned only after stability verified.

support-bot: Incident note: customers impacted: 4 Dedicated tenants in EU had failed onboarding jobs; 12 hosted customers reported increased 5xx for auth token issuance window 10:02-10:12 UTC. Escalation: severity increased to Sev2.

maya: staging rollout succeeded, services booted within expected time. No regression observed.

sam: starting prod canary rollout to 10% pods now. Monitoring logs for any sign of degraded cryptographic ops.

(5m later)

sam: canary is green. no more signing errors on those nodes. Rolling rest of cluster with 1 pod at a time.

(12m later)

jack: bulk rollout complete. Verified metrics for signing_errors back to baseline (<0.1%).

infra-ops: GCP support update: internal control plane experiencing transient overload due to region routing change. They've deployed mitigation and are recommending customers apply retry/backoff and caching. They also provided a request ID list for our telemetry to correlate: [req-9a3f, req-4b7c].

maya: summary for support and customers: 10:02-10:12 UTC — KMS 503s causing startup signing failures and token issuance 5xx spikes. Root cause: GCP KMS control-plane overload in eu-west1. Impact: Dedicated onboarding jobs failed for 4 tenants, hosted token issuance saw short spike of 5xx affecting 12 customers. Mitigation: toggled REDWOOD_KMS_FALLBACK=startup-allow, increased retries/timeouts, rolled canary, provider mitigation.

sam: follow-ups: 1) Update runtime docs with emergency fallback workflow and env var. 2) Add automated runbook step to enable cached fallback with one CLI command in platform runbooks. 3) Add telemetry alert to detect KMS control-plane 5xx vs client-side timeouts.

maya: I'll draft customer comms and a quick incident timeline. tagging @infra-ops for postmortem.

support-bot: next steps logged. assigning to: maya (incident lead), infra-ops (postmortem), sam (runtime patch + docs), devops-ana (deploy playbook).

jack: minor note: we should consider implementing an internal short-lived RSA signing key rotated daily so we don't rely on single KMS call at startup for bootstrapping. Will sketch design in eng-runtime channel.

maya: thanks all. closing pager but keeping thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
